Received NOID for Post-Completion OPT because USCIS thinks my unpaid student organization role was unauthorized employment — I recently received a Notice of Intent to Deny (NOID) on my F-1 Post-Completion OPT I-765 and I’m looking for experiences from anyone who has dealt with something similar. The unusual part is that USCIS explicitly states in the NOID that the record establishes that I am eligible for employment authorization under the C03B Post-Completion OPT category. However, during their background/social-media review, USCIS found a LinkedIn entry where I listed a student leadership role in a university student organization/hackathon under my Experience section. USCIS interpreted that LinkedIn entry as possible unauthorized employment because I never had CPT or OPT authorization for that activity. The role was actually: * part of a university student organization; * completely voluntary/extracurricular; * unpaid; * no wages or salary; * no stipend; * no W-2 or 1099; * no employment contract; * no payroll; * no employee benefits; * performed while I was a student as part of organizing/maintaining projects for the student organization. I used a leadership title on LinkedIn, which apparently made it look like employment even though it was just a student-organization leadership position. USCIS is now asking me to provide a complete employment history and evidence addressing maintenance of F-1 status. They requested things such as employer letters/pay records if applicable, bank statements, W-2s, school enrollment evidence, transcript, tuition records, course information, and DSO/Registrar documentation. Since there are obviously no pay stubs/W-2/1099/employment documents for this student organization because I was never employed by them, I’m planning to submit: 1. A signed letter from the student organization/university-affiliated leadership confirming that it is a university student organization and that my role was completely voluntary and unpaid, with no payroll, wages, stipend, W-2/1099, benefits, or employment agreement. 2. A personal declaration explaining the role, duties, dates, and why it appeared under LinkedIn “Experience.” 3. DSO/Registrar documentation confirming my full-time F-1 enrollment and relevant SEVIS/OPT history. 4. Official transcript/enrollment verification. 5. Tuition/payment records and requested bank statements. 6. IRS wage/income records if available to further show that this organization never paid me. 7. Public/university documentation establishing that the organization is actually a university student organization rather than an employer. Has anyone here received a NOID specifically because USCIS interpreted an unpaid student organization / volunteer leadership role from LinkedIn as unauthorized employment? If so: * What evidence did you submit? * Did a letter confirming no compensation / no employment relationship resolve it? * Did USCIS approve your OPT after the NOID response? * Did you submit bank statements and IRS Wage & Income Transcripts? * How detailed was your personal declaration? * How long after responding to the NOID did USCIS make a decision, especially with Premium Processing?
